data.description: Runs Python for any model, local or cloud: a working directory kept for the session and deleted after it, the network off, each run bounded -- Apogee's code-execution server
data.name: code-exec

data.description: Apogee's own read-only tools, served on stdio by apogee mcp serve for another MCP host (a desktop assistant, an editor)
data.name: self
data.provides: the read-only native tools: files, git, notes, document search, graph navigation; the status reads: models_list, models_status, train_status, train_versions, check; and complete, where the config lists it under a local backend's mcp_serve
data.refusal: 'self' is Apogee's own tools, served for another MCP host: registered into Apogee it would serve Apogee the tools it already has natively. Give another host its entry instead (apogee mcp presets)

data.description: Xcode's own tools for any model: build, run, tests, previews, documentation search, the issue navigator, file reads and writes -- served by Xcode 26.3 or later through xcrun mcpbridge
data.name: xcode
data.note: Xcode answers only while it runs with your project open, and with its Settings › Intelligence › Model Context Protocol › "Allow External Agents to Use Xcode Tools" on. The first connection asks you in Xcode to allow this apogee: Xcode approves an agent by its code signature and its binary's hash, and Apogee's macOS builds are ad-hoc signed, so Xcode asks again after every install or update.
data.provides: Xcode's tools as Xcode lists them: BuildProject, GetBuildLog, RunAllTests, XcodeRead, XcodeListWindows and the rest
